cards.text: Jesus is teaching beside the sea again, and the crowd gets so big that He gets into a boat and sits in it while everybody crowds the shore. He teaches them many things in parables. Friend, the biggest crowd I ever drew was six cookie cutters on a kitchen counter.
Jesus opens with one word: "Listen!" A farmer goes out to sow his seed, and just like my sprinkles, it doesn't all land in one place.

cards.question: Some of the farmer's seed falls along the path, and the ___ come and devour it.

cards.text: Some seed falls on rocky ground. There's not much soil there, just a thin layer over the rock.

cards.question: The seed on the rocky ground comes up slowly because the soil is so shallow.
When the sun rises, the seedlings on the rocky ground are scorched and wither. Why?

cards.text: Other seed falls among thorns. And those thorns grow up right alongside the seedlings.

cards.question: In the farmer's field, the thorns grow up and ___ the seedlings, and they yield no crop.

cards.text: Still other seed falls on good soil. After the path, the rocks and the thorns, I bet this farmer is holding his breath.

cards.question: On the good soil, the farmer's seed sprouts, grows up and produces a crop.

cards.text: One bears thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another a hundredfold. Friend, if my dough came out a HUNDRED times bigger, I'd need a bigger planet.
Then Jesus says, "He who has ears to hear, let him hear." Later, when He's alone with the Twelve, His closest disciples, and the others around Him, they've got something to ask.

cards.question: When Jesus is alone with the Twelve and those around Him, what do they ask Him about?
Jesus tells the Twelve and those around Him that to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables. What does He say has been given to this group?

answers.text: The mystery of the kingdom of God
The keys of the kingdom of heaven

cards.text: Then Jesus quotes words from the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 6:9-10) about people who "may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding…"

cards.question: In the words Jesus quotes, what might happen otherwise?

answers.text: They might turn and be forgiven
They might go and tell others

cards.text: Still alone with the Twelve and those around Him, Jesus asks if they don't understand this parable, and if not, how they'll understand any of the parables. Friend, that's me with a new oven manual: if page one loses me, page forty is NOT happening.
Then Jesus explains the parable, starting with the farmer: "The farmer sows the word."

cards.question: Some people are like the seeds along the path. What happens as soon as they hear the word?

answers.text: Satan comes and takes it away
They argue it out of their heads

cards.text: Satan, the devil, takes the word away just like those birds on the path. Then come the rocky-ground people, who hear the word and at once receive it with joy.

cards.question: The rocky-ground people have no root. What makes them fall away?

answers.text: Trouble or persecution over the word
Growing bored of the same message
Finding a new teacher they prefer

cards.question: When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, the rocky-ground people fall away slowly over many years.

cards.text: Then the thorns. These people hear the word too, and friend, I know what it's like to get buried: I spent YEARS under takeout menus in a junk drawer.
Jesus names what comes in: the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desire for other things. They come in and choke the word.

cards.question: In the thorny-ground people, the word ends up unfruitful.

cards.text: Then Jesus gets to the last group, the ones like the seeds sown on good soil. Friend, THIS is the one I've been waiting for.

cards.question: The good-soil people hear the word. What else does Jesus say they do?

answers.text: Receive it and produce a crop
Keep it and tell no one

cards.text: Jesus keeps going. He asks, "Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed?"

cards.question: Nobody brings in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed. Jesus says you set it on a ___.
Right after the lamp, Jesus says some things that are concealed will stay hidden forever.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear." And He goes on: "Pay attention to what you hear."

cards.question: Jesus says that with the measure you use, it will be measured to you. What else does He say?

answers.text: Even more will be added to you
Nothing more will be added to you
Less will be given back to you

cards.question: Jesus says whoever has will be given more. What about whoever does not have?

answers.text: Even what he has will be taken away
He will be given a little to start
He will be given exactly what he needs

cards.text: Jesus has another one: the kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground. Then the man just sleeps and wakes, night and day, and friend, I can't even leave a batch in the oven without staring through the glass the WHOLE time.

cards.question: As the man sleeps and wakes night and day, he knows exactly how the seed sprouts and grows.
In this parable about the kingdom of God, the earth produces the crop all by itself.
In what order does the man's crop grow?
As soon as the grain is ripe, the man swings the ___, because the harvest has come.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, "To what can we compare the kingdom of God?" His answer is a mustard seed.

cards.question: Jesus calls the mustard seed the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.

cards.text: Now watch what happens once that mustard seed is planted. Friend, I came out of a 25-cent bin, so I am ROOTING for this little guy.

cards.question: What does the tiny mustard seed grow to be?

answers.text: The largest of all garden plants
A small bush in the corner

cards.question: The mustard plant puts forth great branches, so that the cattle of the field rest in its shade.

cards.text: Birds AGAIN, friend: on the path they ate the seed, and here they nest in the shade of what a seed grew into. With many such parables, Jesus spoke the word to them, "to the extent that they could understand."

cards.question: Jesus doesn't tell them anything without using a parable. What does He do privately with His own disciples?

answers.text: He tells them even more parables
He asks them to explain to Him
